formula.en: The first philosophers look for a single natural origin of the world instead of myths
The world is ordered by number and harmony, and the soul is immortal and reborn
Being is one and unchanging; motion and plurality are illusions of the senses
Order in the state begins with cultivating the noble person and respect for elders
Life is full of suffering, it has a cause, and liberation from it is possible
Paid teachers of wisdom and rhetoric: truth and law depend on people
The world is made of indivisible particles, atoms, moving in the void
Impartial care for all and common benefit instead of lavish rituals
Happiness lies in virtue and living by nature, free of wealth and convention
Follow the Dao, the natural way of things, and act through non-action
The state rests on strict laws, rewards and punishments, not on virtue
True reality lies in eternal Forms; the visible world is only their shadow
Aristotle's school: knowledge starts from experience and is ordered by logic
Nothing can be known for certain: suspend judgement and find peace
The goal of life is pleasure understood as peace of mind and freedom from pain
Live by nature and reason: only your own judgements are in your power
The Indian school of logic: true knowledge comes from valid means of knowing
The Church Fathers bring Christian faith together with Greek philosophy
The Buddhist "middle way": things have no essence of their own — all is empty
Everything flows from the ineffable One, and the soul can return to it
The Buddhist "consciousness-only" school: the world we perceive is made by the mind
Awakening comes not from books but from directly seeing one's own nature in meditation
The self and the ultimate reality, Brahman, are one and the same
Islamic theology that defends doctrine with rational argument
Arabic-language philosophers develop Aristotle and the Neoplatonists and pass them on to Europe
Confucianism renewed in answer to Buddhism and Taoism: the world is principle and energy
Only individual things exist; general concepts are just names
The philosophy of medieval schools: reason uses logic to clarify faith
Reviving classical learning, with a focus on human dignity and earthly life
All knowledge comes from experience: at birth the mind is a blank slate
Certain knowledge comes from reason, not the senses: "I think, therefore I am"
"Dare to use your own reason": reason, liberty and progress
The world as we know it is shaped by the activity of mind and spirit
The right action brings the greatest happiness to the greatest number
Only scientific knowledge based on experience is reliable; metaphysics is a stage to outgrow
Truth is grasped by intuition, in unity with nature, without intermediaries
A search for integral knowledge in which faith, reason and life are inseparable
Existence precedes essence: each person chooses what to become
History is driven by class struggle, and society is shaped by how people produce
The meaning and truth of an idea are tested by its practical consequences
Humanity should unite, overcome death and go out into space
"Back to the things themselves": describing experience as it is given to consciousness
Philosophical problems are solved by clear analysis of language and logic
Japanese philosophers join Western thought with the Buddhist idea of "nothingness"
Meaning arises not in things themselves but in the system of relations between them
Only what can be verified by experience or logic is meaningful
Black intellectuals assert the worth of African culture against colonialism
Incredulity towards grand narratives: truth, reason and the self are historically shaped
